title: 01 · Base class + derived class
when: Create Person with a name, then Student with an ID. Initialize the base from the derived constructor and provide getters.
use: Student s("Ada", 42);
change: Replace Person/Student and their data with the types in the question.
watch: A derived class cannot directly read private base fields; use the base getter.
expected: Name Ada; ID 42.

title: 02 · Abstract Shape + area
when: Create an abstract Shape with getArea(), then implement Rectangle and Circle. Call both through Shape pointers.
parts: Makes getArea pure virtual and Shape abstract.
The signature must match the base, including const.
Dispatches to the actual object’s method.
change: Replace getArea with draw, cost, volume or the requested operation.
watch: The local objects are borrowed; do not delete &r or &c. A virtual destructor permits deletion through a base pointer when objects are allocated with new.
expected: Total area is approximately 24.5664.

title: 03 · Protected data + override
when: Create Account with a protected balance and virtual monthlyChange(). Derive SavingsAccount that adds interest.
parts: Derived methods can access balance; outside callers cannot.
Calls through Account* select the derived override.
change: Replace the balance/rate fields and update rule.
watch: Do not redeclare balance in the derived class; that would create a different field.
expected: Balance changes from 100 to 105.

title: 04 · Extend a base method
when: Create Device::reset() to clear a reading. Override reset in Sensor to also clear its error count, while reusing the base reset.
use:
Sensor sensor(12, 3);
sensor.reset();
change: Use this pattern when the question says extend existing behavior.
watch: Calling reset() unqualified inside itself would recurse.
expected: Reading and error count both become 0.

title: 05 · Define derived methods outside the class
when: Declare Shape and Rectangle, then define Rectangle’s constructor and getArea outside its class.
use: Rectangle rectangle(5, 6);
change: Move declarations to a guarded header and definitions to a .cpp including that header.
watch: Repeat const, but not override, on the outside definition.
expected: Area is 30.

title: 06 · Generic base + generic derived class
when: Create a generic BuildingG<T> storing coordinates. Derive HouseG<T> with an owner, and access an inherited coordinate.
use:
HouseG<double> h(3, 6, "Ada");
double x = h.getX();
parts: Pass the same chosen type to the base class.
Construct the base before initializing this class’s fields.
Access a member inherited from a dependent template base.
change: Replace coordinate and owner fields with the requested generic data.
watch: Use this-> for inherited dependent members; keep template definitions in the header.
expected: Inherited x is 3; owner is Ada.

title: 07 · Build a singly linked list
when: Implement IntSLList with addToHead, addToTail and deleteFromHead; handle an empty list and the final removal.
parts: info stores the integer; next links to the following node.
First and last node; both null when empty.
Update links, then update the relevant end pointer.
Save the value and node, update links, delete the old node, return the value.
change: Preserve head/tail/next updates; change info’s type when required.
watch: deleteFromHead requires a nonempty list. Both end pointers must become null after the last removal.
expected: First removal is 10; remaining order is 20, 30.

title: 08 · Traverse and count nodes
when: Add a const countNodes() method that traverses without changing head.
parts: Moves to the following node without moving head.
change: Replace ++count with a sum or another read-only operation.
watch: Do not advance head when you only mean to traverse.
expected: count is 2; counting does not remove any nodes.

title: 09 · Search for a value
when: Add isInList(int el). Return true for a match and false for a missing value or an empty list.
parts: Check the current node before moving on.
Only report failure after all nodes have been checked.
change: Change the equality test to match the requested condition.
watch: Returning false inside the first loop iteration stops the search too soon.
expected: found is true because 9 is present.

title: 10 · Delete the tail
when: Add deleteFromTail() to a singly linked list. Find the predecessor and handle the one-node case.
parts: Singly linked nodes have no prev pointer; walk from head.
change: Use the same predecessor search when removing a node by position.
watch: Requires a nonempty list. Never read tail after deleting it.
expected: last is 2; the remaining node stores 1.

title: 11 · Delete the first matching node
when: Implement deleteNode(el). Support deleting the head, middle, tail or only node, and leave the list unchanged if absent.
parts: Track the predecessor and candidate node.
There is no predecessor; update head directly.
The predecessor becomes the new tail.
change: Change the comparison to remove according to another condition.
watch: This removes the first match, not all duplicates. It is a simplified adaptation of deleteNode in the supplied list.
expected: The remaining list is 1 → 3.

title: 12 · Reverse links in place
when: Reverse the singly linked list without creating new nodes. Update both head and tail.
parts: Preserve the original next link before overwriting it.
Old head becomes tail; final previous becomes head.
change: Use the three-pointer pattern for any singly linked node type.
watch: An extension exercise built from the course node layout, not a copied slide solution.
expected: The list becomes 3 → 2 → 1.

title: 13 · Build Lab 6 Stack<T>
when: Implement push, pop, top, size and isEmpty using StackNode, topOfStack, theItem and count.
parts: A node holds one item and the link below it.
The top node and the current item count.
Create a node, link to old top, move top, increment count.
Save the item, advance top, delete the old node, decrement count, return item.
Inspect without removing; empty access throws StackException.
change: Choose the stored type; keep the Lab 6 function names and return types.
watch: pop returns the item. Empty pop/top throw StackException. Cleanup/copy protection are study additions.
expected: removed is 20; top is now 10; size is 1.

title: 14 · Clear and reuse a stack
when: Add clear() to release all nodes and leave the stack reusable.
parts: Reuses count updates and node deletion.
change: Use clear in a reset operation when the question requires it.
watch: Clearing nodes containing raw pointers does not delete the pointed-to objects.
expected: The cleared stack is reused with one item, 3.

title: 15 · Use a stack to reverse text
when: Push the characters of a string, then pop them to build the reversed string.
parts: The last character ends up on top.
change: Replace characters with another sequence type for reversal.
watch: The stack is consumed by this algorithm.
expected: reversed is "edoc".

title: 16 · Check balanced parentheses
when: Use Stack<char> to validate ( and ). Ignore other characters.
use: bool valid = balanced("(a+(b*c))");
parts: Needs an opener; otherwise reject immediately.
change: To support [] and {}, store each opener and compare its type with the closer.
watch: This example handles parentheses only. It is a practice application of the lab stack.
expected: valid is true; ")(" and "(()" would be false.

title: 17 · Pass stacks by reference
when: Write transfer(source, destination) to move all items using pop and push. Explain the resulting order.
parts: Operate on the original stacks without copying owned nodes.
change: Use a temporary second stack if you need to restore an order.
watch: The destination need not be empty; transferred items are placed above any existing items.
expected: source is empty; destination pops 1, then 2, then 3.

title: 18 · Combine inheritance + Stack<Shape*>
when: Store derived shapes in a stack of base pointers. Pop each shape, call its virtual method, and delete it.
parts: Stores pointers because Shape is abstract.
Uses the Rectangle implementation through Shape*.
pop deletes the node; delete shape releases the owned object.
change: Use the lab draw() operation instead of getArea() if requested.
watch: Assumes processing does not throw; a robust throwing application needs an explicit cleanup/ownership strategy.
expected: Total area is 26; nodes and shapes are released.

title: 19 · Build a queue using linked nodes
when: Implement a generic queue without std::list. Insert at the tail and remove from the head.
parts: Link at tail; the first insertion also sets head.
Remove head; the last removal clears tail.
Manual-node adaptation combining IntSLList links with enqueue/dequeue naming; the supplied ListQueue instead uses std::list.
change: Change the stored type with LinkedQueue<T>. Keep both empty-state pointer updates.
watch: This is a clearly labeled manual-node adaptation, not the instructor’s exact ListQueue implementation.
expected: first is 10; the remaining value is 20.

title: 20 · Course ListQueue<T>
when: Implement the supplied queue wrapper using std::list, enqueue, dequeue, front and isEmpty.
parts: The standard list manages the linked nodes.
Read front, pop_front, then return the saved value.
Inspect the oldest item, test emptiness, or remove all items.
change: Use this version only when standard-library list is allowed.
watch: front and dequeue require a nonempty queue.
expected: first is 10; front is then 20.

title: 21 · Course circular ArrayQueue<T, size>
when: Implement wraparound enqueue/dequeue using first, last and storage; -1 means empty.
parts: Oldest and newest occupied indexes; -1 marks empty.
Check full, wrap last if needed, store the value.
Save the front value; reset if it was the last item, otherwise advance/wrap first.
change: Change capacity and element type. Keep last as the last occupied slot.
watch: A different queue design may define rear as the next free slot; do not mix conventions.
expected: The queue is full again and dequeues 2, 3, 4.

title: 22 · Queue objects in arrival order
when: Create a Job struct with an ID and duration. Enqueue jobs and process them FIFO.
parts: Groups the fields of one queued item.
change: Use Student, Request or PrintJob with the fields in the question.
watch: Use -> only for pointers; next here is an object and uses a dot.
expected: next has ID 101 and duration 2.5; job 102 is still queued.

title: 23 · Move the front item to the back
when: Write a generic rotate function for a queue. Keep the queue unchanged when empty.
parts: Move the first item behind the others.
change: Repeat rotation the required number of times for a round-robin exercise.
watch: Guard the empty case before calling dequeue.
expected: The queue order becomes 2, 3, 1.

title: 24 · Reverse a queue using a stack
when: Write reverseQueue(q) using only queue operations and a temporary linked stack.
parts: Drain FIFO items into a LIFO stack.
Pop reversed values back into the queue.
change: Use a template function if asked to support types other than int.
watch: The function modifies the original queue; pass it by reference rather than copying raw-node ownership.
expected: The queue order becomes 3, 2, 1.
